title: Last night's estimate is still there just after midnight
replays: Bench row B09 and the 15 Nov 2026 class at midnight: on v5.1.1 the owner's day switches at local midnight and the turns before it fall to the small recent-history share, so a 23:50 estimate followed by two short turns is gone from the 00:05 request. Synthetic evening of the same shape; the estimate was never logged, so only the conversation holds it.

history.text: Morning. Breakfast was porridge made with 60 g oats and 250 ml semi-skimmed milk, plus a banana. Log it please.

Logged as breakfast: porridge (60 g oats, 250 ml semi-skimmed milk) 351 kcal, 18 g protein; banana (medium, 118 g) 105 kcal, 1 g protein. Breakfast total 456 kcal, 19 g protein. Day so far: 456 kcal, 19 g protein against your 1,900 kcal and 120 g protein targets.
Lunch: chicken and avocado wrap from the cafe downstairs, the label said 540 kcal and 32 g protein. Also a small apple.

Logged as lunch: chicken and avocado wrap 540 kcal, 32 g protein (from the label); small apple (150 g) 78 kcal, 0 g protein. Lunch total 618 kcal, 32 g protein. Day so far: 1,074 kcal, 51 g protein, so 826 kcal and 69 g protein left. Protein is the gap so far; a protein-led dinner would close most of it.
Afternoon snack, 2 rice cakes with peanut butter, about a tablespoon in total.

Logged as snack-1520: 2 plain rice cakes 70 kcal, 1.5 g protein; peanut butter, 1 tablespoon (16 g) 94 kcal, 4 g protein. Snack total 164 kcal, 5.5 g protein. Day so far: 1,238 kcal, 56.5 g protein, so 662 kcal and 63.5 g protein left.
Is a flat white better than a latte if I'm watching calories?

Slightly, yes: a regular flat white with whole milk is about 110 kcal and 6 g protein, a regular latte about 190 kcal and 10 g protein, because the latte has more milk. With semi-skimmed milk both drop by roughly a third. If you have one, tell me which and I will log it.
Do you think I'm eating enough protein at lunch on weekdays?

Mostly yes: the cafe wrap gives 32 g of protein, which is about a quarter of your 120 g target, a good share for one meal. The apple adds none, so on days when lunch is the wrap and an apple, the afternoon and dinner have to carry about 70 g between them. Two easy upgrades: swap the apple for a 150 g pot of skyr (about 16 g protein, 95 kcal), or add a boiled egg (6 g protein, 78 kcal). Either brings lunch to about 40 to 48 g, which makes the evening protein gap much smaller.
Is it okay to have a coffee this late, or will it mess with sleep?

A regular coffee at 17:30 can still affect sleep for some people: caffeine has a half-life of about five hours, so roughly half of it is still active around 22:30. If you usually fall asleep easily, a small cup is probably fine; if sleep has been patchy this week, a decaf or a herbal tea is the safer choice. Either way, a decaf with semi-skimmed milk is about 60 kcal and 4 g protein, which fits today's numbers easily. If you do have one, tell me the size and milk and I will log it.
Dinner was chicken curry with rice: about 300 g of curry and 180 g of cooked basmati, plus a small naan. Log it please.

Logged as dinner: chicken curry (300 g) 420 kcal, 38 g protein; cooked basmati rice (180 g) 234 kcal, 4.9 g protein; small plain naan (60 g) 157 kcal, 5.2 g protein. Dinner total 811 kcal, 48.1 g protein. Day so far: 2,049 kcal, 104.6 g protein against your 1,900 kcal and 120 g protein targets: 149 kcal over, with 15.4 g protein still to go.
Glass of red wine, a normal pour, maybe 150 ml.
Logged as snack-1930: red wine (150 ml) 125 kcal, 0.1 g protein. Day so far: 2,174 kcal, 104.7 g protein: 274 kcal over, 15.3 g protein to go.
What could I have later that closes the protein gap with the fewest calories?

For the 15.3 g protein still to go, the leanest options are: plain 0% greek yogurt, 170 g: 100 kcal, 17 g protein; a protein shake with water, one scoop: 120 kcal, 24 g protein; cottage cheese, 150 g: 147 kcal, 16.5 g protein. The yogurt closes the gap for the fewest calories; the shake gives the most protein per calorie.
Had a protein shake with water, one scoop of the vanilla whey.
Logged as snack-2105: vanilla whey protein shake with water, 1 scoop (30 g) 120 kcal, 24 g protein. Day so far: 2,294 kcal, 128.7 g protein: protein target met, 394 kcal over.
Late snack: a bowl of blueberries with skyr, roughly a cereal bowl, the blueberries fill about half of it with a big dollop of skyr. Estimate it, don't log yet.

Estimate, not logged: blueberries about 190 g, 108 kcal, 1.4 g protein; plain skyr about 170 g, 107 kcal, 19 g protein. Bowl total about 215 kcal and 20 g protein, which would take the day to about 2,509 kcal. Tell me the pack sizes and I will log the exact figures.
The blueberry punnet label says 125 g and I ate the whole punnet. The skyr pot is 150 g, I had all of it. Log those.

With the labels: blueberries 125 g, 71 kcal, 0.9 g protein; skyr 150 g, 95 kcal, 16.5 g protein. Bowl total 166 kcal, 17.4 g protein, 49 kcal under my estimate. Logged as snack-2335. The day is at 2,460 kcal and 146.1 g protein.
Any ideas for an evening snack tomorrow that isn't fruit and stays under 150 kcal?

Evening snacks under 150 kcal that are not fruit: plain 0% greek yogurt, 150 g with cinnamon, 88 kcal and 15 g protein; cottage cheese, 100 g on a rye cracker, 135 kcal and 12 g protein; two boiled eggs' whites with a pinch of salt, 34 kcal and 7 g protein; a mug of miso soup with tofu cubes (50 g), about 70 kcal and 6 g protein; a 20 g square of 85% dark chocolate with a decaf, 120 kcal and 2 g protein; air-popped popcorn, 20 g, 77 kcal and 2.5 g protein. The yogurt or the cottage cheese also help protein, which is the target you usually have left by the evening.
Give me a quick review of today before I sleep: totals, protein by meal, and anything to change tomorrow.

Today closes at 2,460 kcal and 146.1 g protein against 1,900 kcal and 120 g. By entry: breakfast porridge with banana 456 kcal, 19 g protein; lunch wrap with an apple 618 kcal, 32 g; the afternoon rice cakes with peanut butter 164 kcal, 5.5 g; dinner curry with rice and naan 811 kcal, 48.1 g; red wine 125 kcal, 0.1 g; the whey shake 120 kcal, 24 g; the late blueberries and skyr 166 kcal, 17.4 g. Protein was strong all day, with dinner and the shake doing most of the work. Calories ran 560 kcal over: the curry dinner with rice and naan was the big one, then the wine and the late bowl. For tomorrow: keep the shake, which closed the protein gap cheaply; move the fruit and skyr earlier so it replaces a snack instead of adding one; and if there is wine with dinner, take a smaller rice portion, about 120 g cooked, which saves about 80 kcal. Breakfast and lunch worked well as they are.
And what's the plan for tomorrow's meals, roughly?

A plan for tomorrow at 1,900 kcal and 120 g protein: breakfast, your usual porridge with 60 g oats and 250 ml semi-skimmed milk plus a banana, 456 kcal and 19 g protein. Mid-morning, plain 0% greek yogurt 170 g with a few berries, about 130 kcal and 17 g protein. Lunch, the cafe chicken and avocado wrap, 540 kcal and 32 g protein, with an apple for 78 kcal. Afternoon, a handful of almonds (20 g), 116 kcal and 4 g protein. Dinner, baked salmon 130 g with 150 g new potatoes and green beans, about 444 kcal and 32 g protein. Evening, the whey shake with water, 120 kcal and 24 g protein. That comes to about 1,884 kcal and 128 g protein, with room for a small treat of about 15 kcal or a splash of milk in coffee. If you have wine with dinner, drop the almonds to stay inside the target.
Make me a shopping list for that plan, I'll go to the supermarket at lunch.

Shopping list for tomorrow's plan, by aisle. Dairy: semi-skimmed milk, 1 litre (porridge and coffee); plain 0% greek yogurt, a 500 g tub (mid-morning, with some left for later in the week); skyr, two 150 g pots if you want a spare for the evening. Fruit and vegetables: bananas, a bunch of five; blueberries, one 125 g punnet; apples, a bag of six; new potatoes, a 750 g bag (150 g for dinner, the rest keeps for the week); green beans, a 200 g pack. Fish: two salmon fillets of about 130 g each (one for tomorrow, one to freeze). Dry goods: porridge oats if the bag is under 300 g; unsalted almonds, a 200 g bag. Protein: check the whey tub, you need one scoop; if it is under a quarter full, add a 1 kg tub. Bakery: skip the bread, the plan has none. Drinks: nothing needed. The wrap comes from the cafe downstairs, so it is not on the list. Roughly 14 items; if you buy the salmon on the fish counter, ask for 130 g fillets so the portions match the plan.
Thanks, good night.
Good night. Everything from today is logged.
One more thing: with a long run on Sunday, should breakfast tomorrow be bigger?

Tomorrow is not the long-run day, so breakfast can stay as planned: the porridge with a banana gives about 456 kcal and 19 g protein, which is plenty for a normal day. Save the bigger breakfast for Sunday: about 60 to 90 minutes before the run, have the porridge with an extra 20 g of oats and a spoon of honey, roughly 560 kcal, and drink 400 to 500 ml of water. After the run, a protein-led meal within an hour (the yogurt with fruit, or eggs on toast) helps recovery. If tomorrow includes a gym session, move the whey shake to straight after it instead of the evening.
